sources.title: RFC 5545 — iCalendar
locator: §3.6.5 VTIMEZONE validity for recurring components (web lines 3471–3478)
§3.8.8.1–.2 IANA and non-standard properties (pp. 139–140; web lines 7496–7558)
sources.observed_operation: Defines UID/RID identity; constructs recurrence set from DTSTART/RRULE/RDATE minus EXDATE; specifies time value forms, DST fold/gap, and time-zone definition references.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: EXDATE takes precedence over RRULE/RDATE and duplicates collapse; DTSTART/RRULE mismatch is undefined. RECURRENCE-ID value type matches DTSTART; when moved, RID remains original scheduled time. TZID-local ambiguous values select first occurrence; explicit gap values use pre-gap offset, while rule-generated nonexistent local instances are ignored and not counted. Absent METHOD, do not assume scheduling transaction. Unknown IANA/X-name value data is preserved without interpretation.
sources.applicability: Primary file-format contract for the scoped weekly, named-zone, single-occurrence edit. Broader syntax is not thereby supported by this importer.

sources.title: RFC 5546 — iTIP
sources.observed_operation: Defines organizer cancellation messages and instance reference behavior for scheduling transactions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CANCEL of one recurring instance includes UID plus RECURRENCE-ID; cancellation of whole series omits RID. METHOD:CANCEL is an iTIP scheduling message and may convey attendee/organizer/sequence data.
sources.applicability: Use to distinguish a file snapshot edit from live invitation cancellation; its notification/negotiation behavior is out of scope.

sources.title: Google Calendar API — Recurring events
sources.version_or_commit: Google Calendar API v3 guide (live documentation; no immutable release commit stated)
sources.observed_operation: Retrieve an instance, update its instance resource; cancellation example sets status=cancelled.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: originalStartTime is the scheduled slot, differs from actual start after move, and uniquely identifies the instance within its series. Instance edits/cancel require authorized API calls.
sources.applicability: Comparator for operation-level identity and separate move/cancel; IDs, auth and API resource semantics do not map directly into .ics.

sources.title: Microsoft Graph — event resource
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Graph REST v1.0 event resource (live documentation)
locator: Properties: cancelledOccurrences, exceptionOccurrences, instances, originalStart, seriesMasterId, type
sources.observed_operation: Defines event object fields and navigation collections for a series master, exceptions and cancelled occurrences.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: type values are singleInstance/occurrence/exception/seriesMaster; originalStart is UTC for an occurrence/exception; exceptions differ in fields and are separate from cancelled occurrences; instances omits cancelled ones.
sources.applicability: Comparator for identity distinctions; its provider IDs and UTC property representation do not replace UID/RID/TZID.

sources.title: Microsoft Graph — event: cancel
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Graph REST v1.0 action (live documentation)
locator: Description, HTTP request, permissions, comment body
sources.observed_operation: POST /events/{id}/cancel cancels event and sends comment to attendees.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Organizer only; an occurrence can be cancelled by supplying its occurrence event ID; differs from Delete because it supports organizer's custom attendee message.
sources.applicability: Shows provider-side cancellation is a permissioned scheduling operation; no analog call or attendee messaging in offline import/export.

sources.title: Microsoft Graph — update event
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Graph REST v1.0 PATCH operation (live documentation)
locator: Notes for updating properties; HTTP PATCH; occurrence-boundary response note
sources.observed_operation: PATCH /events/{id} updates a particular event object; page documents master-vs-instance notification behavior and boundary failure.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: An occurrence cannot move to/before the previous occurrence's day or to/after the following occurrence's day in the documented Outlook exception behavior; master update may notify separately for changed instances.
sources.applicability: Provider-specific comparator only; do not impose Graph's boundary restriction as an RFC rule.

sources.title: Microsoft Graph — list instances
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Graph REST v1.0 method (live documentation)
sources.observed_operation: Lists occurrences and exceptions of a seriesMaster over a specified time range.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Date bounds required; response times are UTC unless Prefer: outlook.timezone supplies another supported zone.
sources.applicability: Comparator for retrieving a target instance before editing; requires authenticated provider access absent from product scope.

sources.title: caldata Rust crate
locator: Crate metadata/version list; owner notes on fork and recurrence implementation; dependencies
sources.observed_operation: Rust parser crate exposes iCalendar parsing modules and recurrence-rule module; project says fork adds strict parsing/accessors and recurrence expansion.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Project notes it is a divergent hard fork of archived ical-rs and includes a slightly modified/copy-pasted rust-rrule implementation to support local-time calculations in UTC. Docs coverage shown as 17.74%; the inspected source does not establish byte-faithful preservation of unknown fields.
sources.applicability: A pinned Rust candidate to prototype for weekly recurrence and zone behavior; not selected, and must be tested for opaque property round-trip, scope limits and release stability.

sources.title: pimalaya/ical Rust repository README
sources.version_or_commit: Unpinned repository main inspected; no release tag/commit established here
sources.observed_operation: Describes parsing/editing/serialization plus syntax tree, recurrence and time-zone components.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Repository claims byte-faithful editing and whole-tree round-trip; current main page is not an immutable released artifact in this record.
sources.applicability: Useful architecture/evaluation lead for raw-tree editing, not a dependency recommendation or proven capability in this experiment.

sources.title: collective/icalendar changelog
locator: 7.3.0 bug-fixes: unknown properties/X-properties; TZID vendor prefix; adjacent URI parameter round-trip note
sources.observed_operation: Release history documents previously changed escaping of unknown/X property values on parse/serialize/jCal round trips, later fixed to preserve values verbatim; also a TZID-prefix issue treated a zone as naive until fixed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This is a Python library history, not evidence of a Rust crate defect; its fixes apply to the stated package version only.
sources.applicability: Concrete implementation-history caution motivating property-bag preservation and regression fixtures before claiming a Rust output is compatible.

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The upstream repository is read-only/archived; downstream caldata notes it forked and diverged.
sources.applicability: Historical parser alternative only; insufficient alone for this recurrence/timezone contract and not preferred for a new implementation.
